entries.title: Bank lending to firms
entries.what: Weighted net percentage of banks reporting tighter credit standards, and higher loan demand, over the past three months.
entries.caveats: A positive standards reading means tightening; a positive demand reading means rising demand.

entries.title: Bank lending for house purchase
entries.what: Weighted net percentage of banks reporting tighter credit standards, and higher demand, for mortgages over the past three months.

entries.title: Systemic stress in euro area markets
entries.what: The ECB's CISS combines stress measures from money, bond, equity, financial intermediary and foreign exchange markets, weighted by how correlated they are.
entries.caveats: A higher reading means more stress; the scale is bounded between 0 and 1.

entries.title: Financial stress by country
entries.what: The ECB's country-level CISS for the four largest euro area economies.

entries.title: Consumers' view of prices over the next year
entries.what: Balance of consumers expecting prices to rise faster minus those expecting them to rise slower or fall, seasonally adjusted.
entries.caveats: A qualitative balance, not a rate of inflation.

entries.title: The ECB's measures of underlying inflation
entries.what: The underlying inflation measures the ECB computes from the HICP.
entries.transform: As published by the ECB, except domestic inflation: 12-month change of the ECB index.
entries.caveats: These measures are published about two weeks after the flash HICP and only for the euro area.

entries.title: Overnight rates follow the deposit rate
entries.what: The volume-weighted overnight unsecured rate banks pay (€STR) against the ECB deposit rate.
entries.caveats: €STR trades a few basis points below the deposit rate because of excess liquidity.

entries.title: The euro against the dollar
entries.what: The ECB's daily euro foreign exchange reference rate against the US dollar, set around 14:10 CET.
entries.caveats: A rise means a stronger euro.

entries.title: The euro against its trading partners
entries.what: Trade-weighted average of the euro against the currencies of 41 trading partners, monthly average.
entries.caveats: A rise means a stronger euro.

entries.title: The Eurosystem balance sheet
entries.what: Total assets in the Eurosystem's consolidated weekly financial statement.
entries.transform: EUR millions divided by 1,000. Weekly periods are dated to the Friday of the ISO week.
entries.caveats: Quarter-end revaluations of gold and foreign currency cause small jumps.

entries.title: Recent momentum in prices
entries.what: Change over the latest three months in the ECB's seasonally adjusted HICP indices, compounded to an annual rate.
entries.transform: ((index_t / index_{t-3}) ^ 4 - 1) x 100 on the seasonally adjusted index (ECB HICP flow, adjustment Y, provider 4F0).
entries.caveats: Seasonal adjustment is the ECB's; short-horizon rates are volatile and are revised when the seasonal factors are re-estimated.

entries.title: Inflation at different horizons
entries.what: Headline, core and services inflation over 1, 3, 6 and 12 months, and the ECB's underlying inflation measures.
entries.transform: n-month annualised: ((SA index_t / SA index_{t-n}) ^ (12 / n) - 1) x 100. Domestic inflation: 12-month change of the ECB's domestic inflation index.

entries.title: Inflation by main component
entries.what: Annual inflation in the four main HICP aggregates.

entries.title: Inflation with and without tax changes
entries.what: The HICP recomputed with tax rates held constant, which shows how much VAT and excise changes move the headline rate.
entries.caveats: Constant-tax data are published with the final HICP only.

entries.title: What adds up to headline inflation
entries.what: Eurostat's contributions of energy, food, non-energy industrial goods and services to annual euro area inflation, with the headline rate.
entries.caveats: Published with the final HICP, so the latest flash month has no contributions yet.

entries.title: Inflation in the largest economies
entries.what: Annual HICP inflation in Germany, France, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands and Poland, with the euro area.

entries.title: Inflation across all euro area members
entries.what: Annual HICP inflation in each of the 21 euro area member states, month by month.

entries.title: Flash estimate and final release
entries.what: Eurostat's flash estimate of headline inflation next to the final figure published about two weeks later.
entries.caveats: The flash estimate is published on the last working day of the month or the first of the next; the final release follows mid-month.

entries.title: Headline and core inflation
entries.what: Annual rate of change of the euro area HICP and of the HICP excluding energy, food, alcohol and tobacco, as published by Eurostat.
entries.caveats: HICP excludes owner-occupied housing costs. Since January 2026 the index follows ECOICOP version 2 (prc_hicp_minr); the euro area series is the fixed EA21 composition.

entries.title: What households expect
entries.what: Median of households' quantitative inflation expectations in the ECB Consumer Expectations Survey, euro area aggregate of the 11 survey countries.
entries.caveats: Households' expectations sit well above measured inflation on average; watch the direction rather than the level.

entries.title: What professional forecasters expect
entries.what: Mean point forecasts of euro area HICP inflation in the ECB's quarterly Survey of Professional Forecasters.
entries.transform: Rolling-horizon series are re-indexed from target month to survey round: target month minus the horizon gives the reference month; the round is the next January, April, July or October survey.

entries.title: What it costs to borrow from banks
entries.what: The ECB's composite cost-of-borrowing indicators for new bank loans to households for house purchase and to non-financial corporations.
entries.caveats: Averages across very different national markets: fixed-rate mortgages dominate in Germany and France, variable rates in Spain, Italy and Portugal.

entries.title: Markets at a glance
entries.what: Latest values of the main free daily euro area market series and their changes over a week and a month.
entries.transform: Value on the latest date against the last value on or before 7 and 30 calendar days earlier.

entries.title: Money and bank lending growth
entries.what: Annual growth of the broad money aggregate M3 and of bank loans to households and to non-financial corporations.
entries.caveats: Loans are adjusted for sales, securitisation and cash pooling (ECB definition).

entries.title: ECB policy rates
entries.what: The three key ECB interest rates since 1999 and the overnight €STR.
entries.transform: ECB change-date series expanded to steps (old value the day before each change, new value on the day), extended to the build date.
entries.caveats: Since March 2024 the MRO-DFR spread is 15 basis points; the DFR is the policy rate.

entries.title: What the bond curve implies for short rates
entries.what: Instantaneous forward rates 6 months, 1 year and 2 years ahead on the ECB's AAA government bond yield curve, against the deposit facility rate.
entries.caveats: A rough proxy. Market-implied ECB paths (€STR OIS, Euribor and €STR futures) are licensed data and are not used.

entries.title: What forecasters assume for the policy rate
entries.what: The mean policy-rate assumption respondents to the ECB's SPF give 3, 6, 9 and 12 months ahead, for the four most recent rounds.
entries.caveats: A survey of assumptions, quarterly; not market pricing.

entries.title: Spreads over the German Bund
entries.what: The extra yield investors demand to hold each government's 10-year bonds rather than Germany's.
entries.transform: Country 10-year yield minus the German 10-year yield, monthly averages (Eurostat irt_lt_mcby_m).
entries.caveats: Monthly averages; intra-month spikes are smoothed out.

entries.title: Staff projections for growth
entries.what: The real GDP growth path in the four most recent staff projection rounds.

entries.title: Staff projections for inflation
entries.what: The HICP inflation path in the four most recent ECB (March, September) and Eurosystem (June, December) staff projection rounds.
entries.caveats: Projections are conditional on market assumptions for rates, oil and the exchange rate at the cut-off date.

entries.title: Slope of the yield curve
entries.what: Difference between the 10-year and 2-year spot yields on the AAA euro area curve.
entries.transform: 10-year yield minus 2-year yield on the same day.

entries.title: Euro area government bond yields
entries.what: Spot yields at 2 and 10 years on the ECB's estimated yield curve for AAA-rated euro area central government bonds (Svensson model), daily.
entries.caveats: A fitted curve, not a single bond. The AAA set changes when ratings change.

entries.title: Ten-year yields by country
entries.what: Ten-year benchmark government bond yields used for the EMU convergence criterion, monthly averages.
entries.caveats: Monthly averages of daily yields, so the latest month lags market moves.
